subject: schema
decision: Cited data is canonical in git as generated JSON (tenants.clean.json, paradata.json, geometry-params.json), reviewed by pull request. Postgres is a derived mirror plus mutable state (users, events, saved tours). Exhibit text and claims are files, approved in review, then seeded.
reasoning: Auditable by anyone without a database, diffable, and open-sourceable as-is. Phase 0 needs no cloud credential. Rejected: database-first (BUILD-PLAN 3.4 as written), because a row in Neon is not reviewable or diffable by a stranger, and the trust argument of this project rests on strangers being able to check the work.

subject: column order
decision: Column order is read from each table's own header row. cnn_t1/cnn_t2: Tenant | SF Leased | Industry | Floor. cnn_t4/t5/t6/t7: Tenant | Square Feet Leased | Floor | Industry. Recorded per building in buildings[].column_order.
reasoning: The header cells differ between the two page generations and the parser asserts the derived order against the lead's eyeballed order, so a drift fails the build. The previous extraction (data/wtc_tenants.json) assumed the t1 order for all six pages, which swapped floor and industry for every wtc4/5/6/7 row (49 rows; e.g. US Airways in cnn_t5 got floor "Transportation"). Rejected: hard-coding one order for all files; rejected: detecting the order from cell contents (a floor code and an industry string are both text).

subject: missing cells
decision: A missing value is encoded in the markup as an empty or ; every data row in all six tables has exactly four cells, no colspan/rowspan. Blank cells become null (industry, sq_ft) or "" (floor_raw) with the raw value kept verbatim.
reasoning: Inspected the HTML rather than the rendered text. "Ann Taylor Loft | 7,200 | CNCR" is really four cells with an empty third cell (industry), so nothing is guessed. Rejected: positional inference from a short whitespace-tokenised row, which is how the earlier extraction worked. A defensive path exists for rows whose cell count differs from the header (all fields null, raw_cells kept, dynamic paradata row); no such row occurred in this capture.

subject: padding rows
decision: Trailing rows whose four cells are all empty are dropped and counted in buildings[].padding_rows_dropped (data/cnn_t1.html: 4; data/cnn_t2.html: 0; data/cnn_t4.html: 2; data/cnn_t5.html: 2; data/cnn_t6.html: 3; data/cnn_t7.html: 2). They are not tenants and do not consume source_row numbers.
reasoning: They are spreadsheet-export padding (identical empty <tr> blocks after the last named tenant). The parser fails if a non-empty row ever follows an empty one, so a genuinely blank tenant inside the list could not be silently dropped. Rejected: emitting them as evidence=unknown rows (they assert nothing about any floor).

subject: floor ranges and lists
decision: floor_raw is split on commas; each token is an integer (kept), an ascending range a-b (expanded inclusively, e.g. "9-11" -> 9,10,11), or a known code (CNCR, LBBY, BSMT, GRND, LL, PLAZ; kept as-is). Source order is preserved; floors are not de-duplicated or sorted. Example: "GRND,1-6,13,18-46" -> GRND, 1..6, 13, 18..46.
reasoning: Expansion is the only interpretive step and it is mechanical; a descending range or a range with a code endpoint goes to floor_unresolved rather than being 'fixed'. Rejected: treating a range as 'some floors between' (the source says leased, not partially leased) and rejected mapping codes to numeric levels (CNCR is not floor 0 in this source).

subject: unresolved floor tokens
decision: Tokens that are not an integer, ascending range, or known code go verbatim to floor_unresolved and are omitted from floors. Count in this capture: 0 row(s).
reasoning: Every floor token in all 329 rows resolved to an integer, a range, or one of the six codes. The lead expected "CINDE" (cnn_t2) to be an unknown floor token; in the markup it is not in the Floor column at all (see P-015). Rejected: adding speculative codes to floor_codes to absorb future tokens.

subject: row wtc2-002 "CINDE"
decision: Kept as its own tenant row exactly as the source has it: tenant cell "CINDE", sq_ft "N/A", industry blank, floor blank, immediately after wtc2-001 "Continental Insurance Company" (40,000 sq ft, industry blank, floor blank). raw_cells attached; evidence stays documented because the row is verbatim from the source.
reasoning: The markup gives CINDE its own <tr> with four <td>s, so it is a listing row, not a floor token of the preceding row. It looks like a truncated second line of the Continental Insurance name (CINDE could be a CoStar abbreviation) but that is a guess. Rejected: merging it into wtc2-001; rejected: moving it to wtc2-001.floor_unresolved; rejected: dropping it. A human reviewer may decide to mark it a parsing artifact of the source export.

subject: sq_ft N/A and blank
decision: sq_ft is an integer only when the cell is digits with optional thousands commas. "N/A" and blank both become null; sq_ft_raw keeps the verbatim cell so the two cases stay distinguishable (blank: wtc2 "Gibbs & Hill"). sq_ft_total per building sums the integers only.
reasoning: N/A means the source did not report a figure, not zero. Rejected: 0 (would corrupt totals and imply a measured value); rejected: imputing from floor count.

subject: evidence level
decision: Every tenant row is evidence=documented. No row is corroborated.
reasoning: The CNN list is a contemporaneous listing (CoStar data, published within days of the date the reconstruction depicts), which is the definition of documented in CLAUDE.md. data/SOURCE.md lists eight tenants as 'validated against independently sourced facts' but names no source for any of them, so nothing can be promoted to corroborated yet; a future claims row with a citation can do that per tenant. Rejected: marking rows with blank floor or N/A sq_ft as reported (the evidence level describes the source, not the completeness of the row).

subject: duplicates and parsing artifacts
decision: Exact duplicate rows (same building and identical four cells): 0. Duplicate tenant names within a building: none. The only row that reads as a possible export artifact is wtc2-002 "CINDE" (P-015). Header rows and padding rows (P-012) are the only <tr>s excluded. "&" is the sole HTML entity in any cell and is decoded to "&"; whitespace inside a cell is collapsed to single spaces.
reasoning: Checked every row, not a sample. The previous file's building field contained header text ("...North Tower Tenant SF Leased..."), an artifact of whitespace tokenising; replaced by cnn_label taken from the Building: ... line above each table. Rejected: normalising tenant name spelling or case (e.g. "Sandler O'Neil" is kept as the source spells it).

subject: original CNN URL
decision: sources[0].url = "http://www.cnn.com/SPECIALS/2001/trade.center/tenants1.html"; per-page URLs in buildings[].source_url. Reconstructed from three strings inside each file: the site-root-relative link "/SPECIALS/2001/trade.center/tenants1.html", Akamai asset paths embedding "www.cnn.com/SPECIALS/2001/trade.center/", and the page's own nav link "tenants<n>.html". Scheme http is assumed (2001).
reasoning: No <base href> and no absolute self-link exist in the files, so the URL is reconstructed rather than read. If any of the three strings were missing the field would be null. Rejected: leaving it null when the path and host are both present in the file. buildings[].source_url is an addition to SCHEMA.md because the source is six pages, not one.

subject: Wayback capture URL
decision: sources[0].archived_url is a map of local file to Internet Archive capture URL, all captured 2001-09-13 between 19:12:34 and 19:43:20 UTC.
reasoning: None of the six files contains a Wayback toolbar or archive comment, so the capture URL could not be read from the bytes. The lead fetched each capture from the raw (id_) endpoint on 2026-09-10 and compared the tenant table cell for cell to the local file; all six were identical, which is the evidence that these captures are the source of the local files. The captures redirect to host www2.cnn.com, which is recorded as returned. Rejected: leaving the field null once the match was confirmed, and rejected: citing the www.cnn.com form of the URL, which is not what the archive serves.

subject: source_row numbering and ids
decision: source_row is the 1-based position among data rows of that building's table, counting neither the header row nor dropped padding rows. id = building id + '-' + source_row zero-padded to 3 digits (wtc1-001 .. wtc1-203).
reasoning: Matches the SCHEMA.md example (Strawberry = wtc1-005, the fifth listed tenant). Rejected: numbering by <tr> index including the header (off by one against the schema) and rejected: sorting by name (ids must be stable against the source order, which is CNN's).

subject: WTC 2 story-height schedule (unresolved, decision deferred to a human)
decision: The generator emits WTC 2 with floor plates only at cited elevations (sub-levels 5 to 1 and the service level from the Tower B drawing index, floor 1 and floor 2 from NCSTAR 1-1 Figure 2-3, and the roof) and no perimeter columns. Floors 3 to 110 are listed as omitted in the manifest. No story schedule was adopted for WTC 2.
reasoning: Neither NCSTAR 1-1 nor 1-2A itemizes WTC 2 stories: searched again on 2026-09-11 (Tower B drawing index pdf p189-191 has no elevations above floor 1; Table G-1 pdf p224 has usage but no elevations; Figure 3-4 pdf p33 letters none). Only the 1,362 ft roof (1-2A pdf p34) and '6 ft taller than WTC 2' (1-1 pdf p71) exist. Rejected: copying the WTC 1 Figure 2-2 schedule to WTC 2, because the towers differ by 6 ft so at least one interval differs and the record does not say which. What a human could decide: adopt the 'story heights of typically 12 ft' that 1-2A pdf p34 (and 1-1 pdf p71, towers.typical_story_height) state for both towers, at evidence level `reported`, constrained to the cited 1,362 ft total, with the 6 ft difference assigned explicitly to a named interval (e.g. the hat-truss or roof zone) and flagged as a modelling assumption. The generator is schedule-driven: adding params named wtc2.story_flN_to_flM / wtc2.height_flN_to_flM / wtc2.height_concourse_to_fl9 / wtc2.height_fl110_to_roof in the WTC 1 pattern builds WTC 2 identically (plates, columns) with no code change. That decision is not made here.

subject: plan side parameter for floor plates
decision: Floor plates, the core centring and the column layout use towers.column_reference_line_spacing (207 ft 2 in., 2,486 in.) as the plan side, not towers.plan_side_approx (207 ft).
reasoning: The report gives 207 ft as 'approximately' and 207 ft 2 in. as the exact column-reference-line spacing, and the 6'-11" + 58 @ 3'-4" + 6'-11" column layout on Figure 2-3 sums to 207'-2" exactly, so the exact value is the one the columns need. Rejected: 207 ft (a rounded restatement of the same dimension). The generator checks the two agree to the foot and fails otherwise. Caveat carried from the params file: reference lines do not necessarily coincide with column centroids.

subject: corner chamfer
decision: Floor plates are full squares to the column reference lines; no corner cut is modelled. The 6 ft 11 in. 'chamfer' enters only as the offset from each reference line to the first column line, so the corners carry no column.
reasoning: The cited 6'-11" is dimensioned on Figures 2-3 and 2-15 from the reference line to the first column line; no figure dimensions the slab edge at the corner, and the corner member section is unresolved (towers.corner_column_detail). Rejected: cutting the plates at 45 degrees across the two 6'-11" offsets, which would assert a slab shape the record does not state.

subject: floor 2 elevation conflict (332 ft vs 329 ft 3 in.)
decision: Floor 2 is placed at EL. 332 ft (NCSTAR 1-1 Figure 2-3, towers.floor_2_elevation) for both towers.
reasoning: NCSTAR 1-2A pdf p67 puts a spandrel-splice joint 'at elevation 329 ft 3 in. (floor 2)', but that number is a spandrel centreline used to define model joint coordinates, while Figure 2-3 letters 'Floor 2 / EL. 332'' as a floor line on an elevation drawing. A floor plate wants the floor line. Rejected: 329.25 ft, and rejected: averaging. Both values remain in the params file as separate entries.

subject: floor 9 elevation conflict (Figure 2-2 vs Figure 2-8)
decision: Floor 9 is placed at Concourse + 104 ft = EL. 414 ft (NCSTAR 1-1 Figure 2-2, wtc1.height_concourse_to_fl9). Floors 7 and 9 are NOT derived from the Figure 2-8 tree offsets.
reasoning: Figure 2-8 letters offsets from El. 363.00' that put its 'Floor 9' line at 363 + 9'-4" + 11'-4" + 7'-6" + 17'-5 1/2" + 1'-4 1/2" = 410.0 ft, 4 ft below Figure 2-2's 414 ft; neither report reconciles the two. Figure 2-2 is the one continuous story-by-story schedule and its intervals sum to the stated 1,368 ft exactly, so it is used for every floor line above the Concourse. Rejected: the Figure 2-8 derivation (and therefore floor 7, which only Figure 2-8 could give), rejected: averaging. Elevation of floor 7 stays unresolved (towers.floor_7_elevation).

subject: floors with no cited elevation are omitted, not interpolated
decision: WTC 1 floors 3-8, 42, 108 and 109 get no floor plate. WTC 2 floors 3-110 get no floor plate (P-030). Every omission is listed in public/geometry/manifest.json under the building's `omitted` with the param that spans it.
reasoning: Floors 3-8 lie inside Figure 2-2's undivided 104 ft Concourse-to-FL 9 dimension (and 3-6 are 'Core Only (Storage)' with no floor outside the core); floor 42 lies inside the undivided 28 ft FL 41-43 dimension; floors 108-109 inside the undivided 42'-8" FL 107-110 dimension. Rejected: splitting those dimensions equally (28 = 14 + 14, 42'-8" = 3 x 14'-2 2/3"), which is an inference the figure does not make. The viewer must render an omitted floor as a labelled absence, not as a plate.

subject: WTC 2 roof elevation and the 'above ground' datum
decision: WTC 2 roof = floor 1 (EL. 310) + (1,368 - 6) ft = EL. 1,672 ft, citing wtc1.roof_height_above_concourse and wtc1.roof_height_minus_wtc2 (NCSTAR 1-1) and cross-checked against wtc2.roof_height_above_ground = 1,362 ft (NCSTAR 1-2A). The generator fails if the two disagree.
reasoning: NCSTAR 1-1 states the WTC 2 roof only as 6 ft below WTC 1's 1,368 ft 'above the Concourse level'; 1-2A states 1,362 ft 'above ground' and 1,368 ft for WTC 1 under the same phrase, so the reports treat the two datums as the same line without saying so. Rejected: reading 'ground' as the Plaza line (which carries no numeric elevation, towers.plaza_elevation unresolved).

subject: perimeter column section
decision: Each perimeter column is a box 14 in. along the face (towers.perimeter_column_outer_web_width) by 13 1/2 in. deep (towers.perimeter_column_depth), centred on the column reference line.
reasoning: Figure 2-7 letters both plate-to-plate dimensions; the prose 'approximately 14 in. square' is the rounded version. Figure 2-9 Section A-A subdivides the 13 1/2 in. depth as 7" outside and 6 1/2" inside the reference line, but that split is recorded only in a note, not as a parameter, so the column is centred (a 1/4 in. difference at 1:1). Rejected: 14 x 14 (approximate), rejected: the 7/6.5 split without a param. Flanges, inner-web projection, spandrels and cladding are not modelled.

subject: perimeter column vertical extent
decision: Perimeter columns are continuous boxes from the floor 9 line to the floor 107 line (towers.framed_tube_box_column_floor_range '9 to 107'). Nothing is emitted in the tree zone (El. 363 ft to floor 9) or in the hat-truss zone (floor 107 to roof).
reasoning: The 59-column, 3 ft 4 in. pattern is cited 'between floors 9 and 107'. Above 107 the drawing index shows exterior columns exist (Book 4 'Floors 107 to 110 Column and Spandrel Schedule') but no count or spacing is a parameter. Rejected: extending the columns to the roof (asserts the same pattern where the record is silent); rejected: starting them at the Figure 2-8 Level D line (P-034 conflict). Columns are one box per column for the full height, not split per story; per-floor tinting is done on the plates.

subject: base columns omitted (section not cited)
decision: No base columns are emitted below the tree splice. Added unresolved entry towers.base_column_section.
reasoning: Their positions are fully cited (10 ft on centre, 18 bays, 6'-8" end bay, 6'-11" to the corner line, Figure 2-3) but no plan section is lettered anywhere in NCSTAR 1-1 or 1-2A (checked Figures 2-3, 2-8 and 1-2A Figure 2-6 on 2026-09-11). Rejected: reusing the 14 in. perimeter section for the base columns (a dimension transfer the record does not support); rejected: any placeholder width. Where to look: NCSTAR 1-2A Appendix C Drawing Book 1 column types, NCSTAR 1-3. Until then the base of each tower shows plates and the core only, which the manifest states.

subject: core placement and extent
decision: The core is one box, approximately 135 ft by 87 ft, centred on the plan, long axis east-west for WTC 1 and north-south for WTC 2, from the foundation level (EL. 242) to the roof line.
reasoning: Centring follows from the cited approximate core-to-wall distances: 36 + 135 + 36 = 207 and 60 + 87 + 60 = 207, which the generator checks against the plan side to the foot. Rejected: offsetting the core from one wall by exactly 36 / 60 ft, which would put a 2 in. asymmetry into the model that no source states. Core columns, walls, shafts and the exact rectangle stay unresolved (towers.core_plan_dimensions_exact).

subject: floor plate thickness and vertical convention
decision: Every plate (sub-levels, floors, roof) is drawn 4 in. thick (towers.truss_floor_slab_thickness) with its top face on the cited floor line.
reasoning: Plates are visual markers of cited floor lines, not slab models. The 4 in. lightweight slab is cited for tenant floors outside the core; the mechanical-floor (5 3/4 in. + 2 in. topping) and above-mezzanine (7 3/4 in.) thicknesses are cited but not for every level, and concourse / sub-level slab thicknesses are not stated, so one thickness is used throughout and the manifest says so. Top-of-slab as the floor line follows NCSTAR 1-2A's statement that reference elevations 'corresponded to the elevations of the top of the concrete floor' (pdf p32). Rejected: per-floor thicknesses (incomplete record), rejected: inventing a lobby slab.

subject: below-grade levels, naming and the Tower A drawing index
decision: Six plates per tower below the Concourse, named <tower>_sublevel_5 .. _sublevel_1 and <tower>_service_level after the NCSTAR 1-2A drawing-index labels. WTC 2 uses the Tower B index lines (pdf p189). WTC 1 uses the Tower A index lines located on pdf p181 on 2026-09-11 and added as wtc1.sublevel_*_elevation_drawing_index; its sub-level 4 (SA-3) carries no elevation in the index, so 253 ft comes from towers.level_b5_elevation (1-2A pdf p67).
reasoning: The params file said the Tower A index had not been found; it is on pdf p181 (printed p149) with the same elevations (242 / 264 / 274 / 284 / 294). Naming conflict recorded, not resolved: NCSTAR 1-1 calls EL. 294 'Sublevel 1', Table G-1 calls it 'B1', the drawing index calls it 'service level' and EL. 284 'sub-level 1'; the B-n and sub-level-n numberings differ by one. Node names follow the drawing index because it is the only labelling that gives every level a number. Rejected: summing Figure 2-3's 11' + 4 @ 10'-0" bays (reaches 293, not 294; the discrepancy is on towers.bracing_bay_bottom_height).

subject: coordinate frame of the .glb files
decision: glTF metres, +x east, +y up, -z north; origin at the centre of the column-reference-line square; y = 0 at the floor 1 (Concourse) line, EL. 310. Each tower is in its own local frame.
reasoning: The drawings use a project datum (Concourse = 310 ft) that is not sea level; subtracting the cited floor 1 elevation puts the Concourse at y = 0 so the viewer does not float the towers 94 m up. Tower-to-tower spacing and site position are unresolved (complex.tower_positions_and_spacing), so no offset between wtc1.glb and wtc2.glb is baked in. The east-west / north-south core orientations are the only compass-dependent geometry; north = -z matches the three.js convention the viewer uses. Rejected: absolute datum elevations as y.

subject: antenna omitted
decision: No antenna is modelled on WTC 1. WTC 2 has none (wtc2.antenna_built = false).
reasoning: Only the 360 ft height is cited (wtc1.antenna_height); base elevation above the roof, mast radius / taper and plan position are not (unresolved wtc1.antenna_geometry). A cylinder needs a radius. Rejected: a placeholder mast, which would be an uncited dimension in the most visible place on the model.

subject: perimeter column layout along each face
decision: Per face: 59 columns at 40 in. on centre, the first 6 ft 11 in. from the column reference line at each end, on all four faces, columns centred on the reference line. Generator checks 83 + 58 x 40 + 83 = 2,486 in. and fails otherwise.
reasoning: From Figure 2-3 ('58 @ 3'-4" = 193'-4"' with 6'-11" at each end) and Figure 2-15 (column 401 / 301 at 6'-11"). The four faces are assumed identical because the report describes 'each building face' the same way; the 100/200/300/400 series designations are not carried into node names because Figure 2-15 has no north arrow. Rejected: numbering instances by column series (would assert a compass mapping the figure does not give).

subject: WTC 2 story heights: modeling assumption adopted
decision: WTC 2 floors 3 to 110 are modeled 12 ft apart above the cited floor 2 line, with a 44 ft remainder from floor 110 to the cited 1,362 ft roof. Every WTC 2 floor elevation above floor 2 carries evidence level reported and renders visibly lighter than WTC 1's documented floors. Supersedes the deferral in P-030 for rendering purposes only; wtc2.story_height_schedule stays on the unresolved list.
reasoning: NCSTAR 1-1 p71 states 12 ft as the typical story height for both towers, so the assumption is anchored to a cited statement rather than invented, but the report itemizes only WTC 1 and the towers differ by 6 ft, so the WTC 2 distribution is not known. Chris Cousins chose this over leaving WTC 2 as a bare core (the alternative offered) because a labeled, lighter, source-anchored approximation is more useful to a visitor than a column, provided the uncertainty is visible in the model and in the manifest. Rejected: copying WTC 1's Figure 2-2 schedule (its 14 ft and 16 ft intervals are WTC 1 specifics); distributing the 44 ft remainder across floors (would silently change a cited 12 ft); labeling the result documented (it is not).
decided_by: Chris Cousins, 2026-09-11, on options prepared by Claude (Fable 5.1)

subject: Interiors: illustration layer permitted, labeled hypothetical
decision: Walk mode may include a generic office fit-out as a separate illustration layer, labeled on screen as a hypothetical reconstruction, toggleable, never mixed with the cited layer. Tenant zones, dimensions, names and citations remain the cited layer.
reasoning: Chris judged that a walkable floor that reads as a workplace communicates the subject (a working commercial district) better than data volumes alone, and that the London Charter's explicit category of labeled hypothetical reconstruction makes this honest so long as the label is persistent and the layers never blend. Rejected: photorealistic interiors presented as reconstruction (fabrication); AI-generated furniture (rule 3); keeping rule 2 as written (the product would stay abstract, which Chris reviewed and found insufficient).
decided_by: Chris Cousins, 2026-09-11, on options prepared by Claude (Fable 5.1)

subject: Walk mode: tenant zone layout on a floor
decision: In Walk mode the leasable ring (plate minus core) is divided into angular slices around the core, one per tenant row the source places on the floor, in source row order, starting at the south face and running clockwise. Each slice's angle is the row's share of the floor's listed square feet, normalised so the slices fill the ring. A row with no square-foot figure gets the smallest listed share on that floor (an equal share if no row gives a figure) and its plaque says 'sq ft not given'. A floor with no row is one ring labeled 'No tenant record in this source.' A floor with one row is one ring carrying that row.
reasoning: The source gives square feet and floor, never a position on the plate, so any arrangement is interpretive; angular slices are deterministic, keep every zone touching both the core and the glass, and make relative size legible at eye height. Normalising to fill the ring means the drawn areas are proportions, not the listed areas: a row that spans several floors is listed with its full figure on each (P-017 convention) and floors can list more or less than the cited approximately 31,000 sq ft column-free area, which the HUD states alongside the listed total. Rejected: rectangular subdivision (needs a packing heuristic that would invent adjacency); leaving unlisted rows out (they are rows in the source); scaling zones to absolute listed area (would leave voids or overlaps the record does not describe); placing tenants by any outside knowledge of where they sat.

subject: Walk mode: illustration layer construction and treatment
decision: The illustration layer permitted by P-047 is built only from procedural boxes and cylinders (desk, two legs, partition, chair seat, back and post), a code-generated carpet tile texture, a ceiling grid of lines and a scatter of thin ceiling tiles. Furnishing sizes are generic constants declared in the code as uncited. Desks sit on a fixed grid inside each tenant zone and are dropped wherever any corner of the cluster would touch the core, the glass line, or the zone boundary, so density follows zone area. The layer uses its own materials (a grayscale-warm stipple texture) and shares none with the cited layer. While on, the HUD shows the fixed label 'Illustration. Furnishings are not a reconstruction.' It is on by default, can be turned off, and the choice is remembered in the browser; a query string ?illustration=off forces it off for one load. Nothing in the layer carries a tenant name.
reasoning: London Charter: a hypothetical reconstruction must be visibly distinguishable from evidence and its status stated. A single stipple palette for every furnishing makes the layer read as a drawing convention rather than a finish, and keeping the cited slab as the visible ceiling (the grid and tiles hang just under it) avoids implying a suspended-ceiling height the record does not give. Rejected: downloaded or CC0 furniture models in this pass (no license record yet); AI-generated assets (rule 3); a drop ceiling at a plausible height (uncited dimension); per-tenant variation of the fit-out (would imply knowledge of a specific tenant's floor).
